stories.story_title: Uncrewed reconnaissance integrated into a live multinational forcible-entry at RED FLAG-Alaska 26-2
verified_facts: RED FLAG-Alaska 26-2 concluded June 12, 2026 at Eielson AFB and JBER.
The 1-40th Cavalry of the 11th Airborne Division ran a joint forcible entry at Donnelly Drop Zone that integrated drone reconnaissance with live TOW and mortar fires in a contested environment.
Over 2,100 service members and 70 aircraft from the U.S., UK, Canada, New Zealand, and Singapore participated.
Held across the Joint Pacific Alaska Range Complex (JPARC).
do_not_assert: Specific 'June 10' date for the forcible entry (DVIDS source 2 places the JFE phase June 3-5; use 'during the exercise, which concluded June 12').
The 1-511th PIR unit transformation in July (unsourced on fetched pages; omit or attribute as reported).
stories.industry_consequence: Defense / autonomous systems: JPARC is functioning as the DoD's cold-environment test bed for uncrewed-systems doctrine, and the requirements written there become the procurement spec UAS vendors must meet.

stories.story_title: Air Force AI data-center RFLP at JBER/Eielson/Clear draws Interior pushback; GVEA grid-cost risk (bids due June 29)
verified_facts: DAF released an RFLP for privately financed and operated AI data centers at JBER, Eielson, and Clear SFS; proposals due June 29, 2026.
In-window reporting June 8 to 11 documented community concerns over permafrost, noise, water, and GVEA grid-cost exposure.
One parcel is reportedly less than a mile from North Pole Middle School.
Five Eielson-area parcels; the RFLP requires the developer to secure its own power, and residents fear costs land 'on the backs of GVEA members.'
No Alaska ratepayer-protection statute is in place (SB 250 not enacted).
do_not_assert: Acreage figure '4,700 acres' / '12 parcels' (unverified). Say 'parcels across three installations'.
stories.industry_consequence: Energy/utility: GVEA and Interior ratepayers face a decision before June 29 on whether to register grid-cost objections, with no Alaska statute preventing cross-subsidization.
stories.frame_note: RFLP landlord/operator frame led 06-11; GVEA cost was support 06-13. Use as supporting test-bed/substrate angle only, NOT as lead.

stories.story_title: GCI deploys Starlink bonded gateways to Bethel, Sitka, Kotzebue, Dillingham
verified_facts: GCI announced June 11 it is deploying Starlink dedicated bonded gateways at Bethel, Sitka, Kotzebue, and Dillingham for multi-gigabit middle-mile capacity.
Extends GCI's 2024 SpaceX reseller agreement; follows operational installs at Unalaska (up to 10 Gbps) and Nome.
GCI exec, verbatim: 'We have long said it takes every tool in our toolkit to serve a state like Alaska.'
do_not_assert: '99%+ uptime' (not confirmed on fetched pages; strip).
stories.industry_consequence: Broadband/telecom: GCI must decide within 12 months whether to route BEAD dollars toward hybrid satellite architecture vs pure fiber after repeated subsea cable breaks.

stories.story_title: Four Alaska ANC subsidiaries land spots on Air Force $4B AETC base-operations IDIQ
verified_facts: June 8: Air Force awarded a $4 billion, 10-year base-operations support IDIQ for AETC to 19 firms (22 offers received).
Four Anchorage ANC subsidiaries: Chugach Intelligence Solutions, Alutiiq Operations Services, Alcyon, Bering Straits Management Services.
Scope includes IT and communications services. Contract runs through June 30, 2036.
AETC bases are in the Lower 48 (OK, TX, AL, AZ, NM, MS); the Alaska tie is corporate ANC ownership, not geography.
stories.industry_consequence: Federal defense IT (ANC subsidiaries): four ANC firms hold multiple-award positions through 2036 to compete for AETC task orders.
stories.frame_note: AI angle thin (base-ops IT/comms), Lower-48 bases. Optional supporting texture only.

stories.story_title: Federal judge voids $100K H-1B fee; Alaska rural districts warn the hiring window may already be closed
verified_facts: June 8: U.S. District Judge Leo Sorokin struck down the $100,000 H-1B visa fee as an unauthorized tax violating the APA.
341 of Alaska's 573 international teachers hold H-1B visas; some rural districts depend on international staff for 50 to 80% of positions.
Alaska Council of School Administrators (Lisa Parady) warns districts will wait-and-watch pending appeal; 1,200+ teaching vacancies statewide.
stories.industry_consequence: Education workforce: rural districts decide by ~August 2026 whether to resume H-1B sponsorships before an appeal could reinstate the fee.
stories.frame_note: AI angle is essentially nil. Do NOT use in an AI-page post unless as a brief workforce aside. Default: omit.

stories.story_title: Great American AI Act draft would preempt state AI-development laws for three years; deployment rules survive
verified_facts: The bipartisan Great American AI Act discussion draft (released June 4-5) imposes a three-year preemption on state laws regulating AI model development; deployment/use, civil-rights, labor, and privacy rules are preserved.
Analysts (DLA Piper, Future of Privacy Forum) confirm the preemption targets development, not deployment.
It is a discussion draft, not enacted (prospective).
do_not_assert: That Alaska's SB 2/HB 239 'would survive' as reported fact; attribute as analysis. No fetched page is Alaska-specific.
stories.industry_consequence: Government/legal: Alaska's window to set developer-facing AI rules narrows; deployment rules survive but development rules would be frozen until ~2029.

stories.story_title: Stak Energy's proposed $500M North Slope private AI data center (DNR comment period)
verified_facts: Stak Energy is seeking a 50-year state land lease near Milepost 390 of the Dalton Highway for a proposed $500 million AI/HPC campus drawing 1 to 3 GW from North Slope natural gas (per late-May reporting).
Alaska DNR opened a public comment period on its preliminary best-interest finding; reporting described the close as 'mid-June.'
do_not_assert: The specific 'June 15' deadline as confirmed fact. All sources dated May 14 / May 26 (out of window). Alaska Beacon URL returned 403.
stories.usage: Background only. If referenced, attribute: 'reported in late May ... comment period expected to close in mid-June.' Do not lead on it.

stories.story_title: Alaska HB 239 AI-CSAM felony provisions (passed May 20, governor action pending)
verified_facts: HB 239 passed 20-0 (Senate) and 39-1 (House) on May 20 and includes felony penalties for AI-generated CSAM.
Governor's office said the bill 'will require careful analysis' (May 20 quote).
do_not_assert: That it was confirmed still unsigned during the June 6-13 window (no in-window source).

validation_summary: Five verified in-window (RED FLAG autonomy, DAF/GVEA data-center RFLP, GCI Starlink gateways, ANC AETC IDIQ, H-1B teacher ruling) plus GAAIA verified-softened. STAK North Slope and HB 239 demoted to background-only (sources out of window). Validator ran clean; no transient failures.
